THR HEALTH OF MR. JOHN BRIGHT. Mr. Bright on Wednesday passed a pleasant day, thus gaining strength, and making satisfactory progress towards re- covery. Dr. Hayle in the afternoon visited Mr. Bright and stated that his condition had improved in every way, and he was now allowed to sit up five or ten minutes every day. In fact the distinguished patient had im- proved so much that the doctor only made one visit on Wednesday, believing that one call per day, and occa- sionally a night visit, would now be sufficient. On Thursday it was stated that Mr. Bright had again passed a good night, and was improving very nicely. Dr. Hayle visited Mr. Bright again on Friday after,noon, and found him still improving. The late Mr. William M'Qualter, hatter, of Trongate, Glasgow, has, with the exception of a few legacies, be- queathed the whole of his estate, £35,000, to the British and Foreign Unitarian Association, for the support and promulgation of the principles of Unitarian Christianity in Scotland.

Mr. W. S. Caine, M.P.' speaking at Blackbu n on Wednesday night, said that if the compensation clauses of the Local Government Bill passed the liquor traffic would receive an endowment of £500,000,000, which would saddle the country with a responsibility almost equal to the entire national debt. If the Government preferred to stand or fall on this question, so far as he was concerned they would have to fall.

MANCHESTER HAY AND STRAW, FRIDAY.—IIay, 70. to ; clover, 70. to Bd. ; wheat straw, 50 to sd; oat straw, 5.0. to 50. per stone of 141 t. LONDON PRODUCE, FRIDAY. Sugar market remains steady • betroot quoted 13s 10 June and 13s 3d July. Coffee generally atmuly. Tea No sales to-day. Rice continues quiet. Cotton market unaltered. Jute steady at late values. Tallow Y.C., 35s spot. Rape oil, 23s ; linseed do., 18s exl to 18s 70. Turpentine, 29s 9a to 30s. Petroleum: American, 50 to 50. LIVERPOOL PROTISIONS, FRIDAY.—Beef rules inactive for fine sorts and steady for lower grades. Pork is firm. For most cuts of bacon there has been a better demand, and prices have a tendency to harden. Hams and shoulders are in improved request, and holders now ask from 6d to is per cwt. more money. Cheese is firmer at unaltered prices. But- ter rules quite nominal. Cable advices from America, re- ceived to-day, quote a decline of Sd per cwt. in the value of bacon.

Mild cured firkins: Superfine, 87s ; fine, 79s ; mild, 78s. Kegs Fine, 765 ; mild, 735. Its the market : 1,300 firkins, 6 kegs, 313 mild. MANCHESTER TRADE, FRIDAY. The market at the opening is steady, but rather dragging. There are more manu- facturers here to-day than is usually the case on Thursdays. Whether this is because of an eager desire to purchase yarn or in order to obtain some business in cloth, they themselves are best able to answer. We do not, however, hear of much in- creased demand, and the market closes dull.

The Liverpool Commercial Banking Company, Limited, Liver- pool, and Messrs. Williams, Deacon, and Co., London, are authorised to receive applications for the undermentioned debentures and share capital. The LIST OF APPLICATIONS will OPEN on Thursday, the 14th day of June, 1888, and will CLOSE on or before Satur- day, the 16th day of June, 1888. EDWARD YOUNG & COMPANY, LIMITED, LIVERPOOL.—Incorporated under the Companies' Acts, 1862 to 1886. Share capital, £150,000 ; debentures, £75,000. Divided into 15,000 ordinary shares of £lO each, £150,000 ; 5 per cent, first mortgage debentures, £75,000 (se- cured as a thateharge upon all the undertaking and property of the Company). . Present issue- -8.500 ordinary shares of £lO each L85,000 Five per cent. first mortgage debentures .. £130,000 Including the allotment to the vendors, applications have been received for £BO,OOO of the above before the registration of the Company. The shares are payable as follows :—£l on application, £3 on allotment, £3 on August 1, and £3 on September 1, rank- ing for dividend as from the dates of payment. Any share- holder desirous of paying in full on allotment will be entitled on such payment to 5 per cent. interest on the amount for the time being not called up. The debentures will be payable —LIO per cent, on application, £2O per cent, on allotment, and £7O per cent. on September 1, ranking for interest as from the dates of payment. Interest on the debentures will be paid half- yearly. DIRECTORS: Samuel Charles Woodward, Esq., Seel-st. Distil- lery, Liverpool, Managing Francis Richmond, Esq, Seel-st. Distillery, Liver- Directors. pool, Rowland Young, Esq., Seel-et. Distillery. Liverpool, And two other Directors, to be appointed by the shareholders at the first general meeting. BANKERS The Liverpool Commercial Banking Company, Limited, Liver- pool. Messrs. Williams, Deacon, and Co., London. SOLICITOIS : Messrs. H. W. Collins, Robinsom Collins, and Drifflehl, Liver- pool. BROKERS Messrs. A. M. drealloch and Co., Liverpool. AUDITORS 'Messrs. Cochran and Walker, chartered accountants, Liver- pool. SECRETARY—Mr. Peter Shallcross Wood. Registered Offices, 11, Seel-st., Liverpool.

DIV kILD YOUNG AND CO., LIMITED, LIVER- E POOL. PROSPECTUS. This Company has been formed for the purpose of acquiring by purchase as a going concern the old-established and well- known business of Edward Young and Co., Liverpool. distil- lers, rectifiers, manufacturers of cordials, and wholesale wine and spirit merchants. The business was established over seventy years ago, and throughout this period a steady and profitable trade has been consistently maintained. The ifirm bears a high reputation, is well known, and has large and extensive dealings with cus- tomers throughout the United Kingdom., and by the extension of co-operative principles and the development of various branches of the trade it is confidently anticipated that a still further large and remunerative .business will be done. In the formation of the Company it is proposed to alter the existing business arrangements as little as possible, the two partners in the firm of Edward Young and Co. having under- taken to continue the management of the business at a re- muneration largely contingent upon the amount of profit made, and the whole of the present experienced staff, some of whom have been with the firm for a considerable time, Laving agreed to continue in the employment of the Company. , The business will be taken over by the Company as a going , concern as from the let day of May, 1888, so that no interrup- tion of the working will occur, and the shareholders may therefore look for a good and immediate return upon the capi- tal embarked in the undertaking from the date of its incor- poration. The books of the firm have been examined by Messer& Coeh- ran and Walker, chartered accountants, Liverpool, froze whose report it will be seen that after providing for debenture inter- est the average profits for the last four years (when the last change in the constitution of the vendors' firm took place, and also for the last 20 years. have been sufficient to pap a dividend of 10 per cent per annum on the present issue of shares.. The profit for the four months ending 30th April last also shows sufficient to pay the same dividend. The vendors, in consideration of £l3o,ooo—as to one-third thereof by the allotment of fully paid-up shares, and/or the issue to them of debentures :of the company, at the option .of the vendors, and as to the balance either in cash or fully-paid up shares or debentures, at the company's option Will transfer to the company the freeholddistillery and premises in Seel-at., Liverpool; the tenant's interest in the Bonded Vaults and premises in Tower Buildings, Liverpool;. and "Armitage's " Tower Garden, Liverpool; the plant, stills, fixed machinery, trade and tenant's fixtures, .utensils, trade marks, .prize medals, the stock in trade, casks, accrued warehouse rents con' bonded goods, book debts, and goodwill of the business. The stock of wines and spirits, ax„ has been valued by Messrs. Unwin and Jaeltaon, cf Liverpool, at £31,276 is 11d. The book debts are of recent contraction, and amount to £55,551 15s 2d, subject to certain discounts, the vendors guar- anteeing the tame to produce :£54,500 at the least, within twelve months. The company will take over the trade liabilities of the firm of Edward Young and Co., and the benefit and liability of all contracts entered into by or enbiehalf of the said firm as from the Ist day of May, 1888. The total liabilities are certified by the vendors not to exceed £23,250. Applicants for shares will be .held to have had notice of all trade contracts, and to have waived their right to be supplied with particulars. The only contracts other than trade contracts which have been made are : (1.) A contract dated thelipth May, 1888. made bebaveen Samuel Charles Woodward and Francis Richmond of the one part, and Peter Shalleross Wood, on behalf of the company, of the other part. This contract is set out in the schedule to the articles of association of the com- pany. (2.) A contract dated the 29th day of May, 1888, and made between the said Samuel Charles Woodward and Francis Richmond of the one part, and the said Peter Shall- cross Wood of the other part. (3.) A contract dated the 29th day of May, 1888,andinade between the said Samuel Charles Woodward and Francis Richmond of the one part, and :Rowland Young of the other part. 4 'The memorandum and articles of association, copies of thee specified contracts, form of debenture, and report of Messrs. Cochran and Walker, can lie inspected at the offices of the sttieitors, or the offices of the Company. •The Directors in allotting shares will at their discretion give preference to customers of the firm and others in the trade, it being desired to give them a beneficial interest there- in, which cannot but add to the future prosperity of the Coin- pony. Zt no allotment be made the deposit will be returned in full, and if the number of shares allotted represent less than those wilier' for the surplus will be credited in reduction of the further sums payable on the shares allotted, and appli- cants shall be bound by such allotment, notwithstanding that the number of shares allotted may be less than those ap- plied for. ApPlication is intended to benaade forthwith for a quotation on the London and Liverpool Stock Exchanges. All expenses in connection with the registration and forma- tion of the Company up to and including allotment will be paid fq,'the vendors. Application for shares should be forwarded to the bankers or the offices of the Company, together with a remittance for the amount of the deposit.

ISHERWOOD seconded, the confirmation of the minutes, which was agreed to. A GIFT. The Wometeortsm MASTMR recorded, with thanks,-R•gift of two baskets of flowers to the inmates by the Rev. Mr. Prescott, of Lttchford. F. SCHOOL FEES. The School Fees Committee reported that fees had been allowed in 12 new and 77 old4cases, tetal 89.—Mr. BLACKHURST moved the adoption of the minutes, which was agreed to.—ln reply to a question, it was stated that the number of fees allowed in the correspondins, period of last year was 71. VACCINATION AND SMALLPDX. The ASSISTANT CLERK mentioned that he had received a memorandum from the Local Government Board pre- scribing new regulations as to vaccination.—Mr. DARBY- SHIRE said he had heard when some miles away from Warrington that there was a case of smallpox—a navvy —in the Infectious Hospital there.—The CHAIRMAN said if there was it must be of a very recent date, as he knew nothing about it. He understood from Mr. Mines that the children at Padgate Schools had been successfully re-vaccinated by the doctor with.the exception of about a dozen who had not taken.—The subject then dropped. APPOINTMENT OF MASTER'S ASSISTANT. , The House Committee reported that 19 applications had been received for the post of master's assistant at the Workhouse, mad that they had selected six of the ap- plicants to appear before the Board.—The CHAIRMAN said the reason they had selected six candidates to ap- pear before the Board was that four of them lived in the town, and the other two not far away.—The six ap- plicants afterwards appeared before the Board in the following order: Mr. W. H. Clegg, Nantwich, aged 20; Mr. J. G. Corlett, Hall-st. Warrington, 30 • Mr. E. Howard, Church-st., Warrington, 24; Mr. A. B. Bailey, 9, Selby-st., Warrington, 22; Mr. James Allison, Church- st., Warrington, 23; and Mr. G. H. Lamb, Altrincham, 23. In the first round of voting Messrs. Clegg, Howard, and Lamb received the highest number of votes; in the second Messrs. Howard and Lamb were retained; and finally Me. Lamb, who is at present engaged as chil- dren s superintendent at the Altrincham Workhouse, was unanimously appointed. This was all the business of public interest.

LATEST NEWS;

The bodies of the young men Finnis and Took, who were drowned off Dover on Whit-Monday, were washed ashore on Friday. CamitEr.—Australians, first innings, 266; Cambridge University, second innings, 31 for the loss of two wickets when the stumps were drawn. , A railway cellision occurred at Stratford, on the Great Western Railway, on Friday morning. Several passen- gers were injured; some seriously. The strike of saw grinders at Sheffield terminated on Friday, the men accepting a compromise between the masters new terms and the old hours of work. The Exchange Telegraph Company understands that Miss Phyllis Broughton has issued a writ for breach of promise of marriage against Viscount Dangan, only son of Earl Cowley. The Board of Trade returns for May show that the im- ports for the month increased by a,419,454, and the exports increased by £2,778,389, compared with the same mcnth last year. Mr. E. Hulse, Conservative member for Salisbury, writing to the Rev. E. Thwaites, of the city, states that he will certainly not vote in favour of any flesh burden being placed on the rates for the purpose of compensating publicans. Lord Salisbury, arrived at Cambridge oa Friday after- noon, and visited the Junior Conservative Club, where ho made a short non-political speech. lathe evening his lordship dined at Trinity College with Prince Albert Victor and other guests. ALLEGED THEFT BY A STATIONMASTER —At Oxford, on Friday, George Taylor Bea,vington, stationmaster at Yarnton station, and Barbara Emily, his wife, were re- manded, charged with stealing a registered letter from a mail bag, and abstracting a £5 note. A CHILD KILLED ON THE HAILWAY.—At a little before one o'clock on Friday, a girl named Annie Stafford, aged 10 years, was killed at the Strimes station by the Mid- land express, which leaves Manchester at 12-10 for Derby. The child had been with a dinner to the Strimes print works, and in attempting to cross the line was caught by the train. - AFFRAY WITH POACHERS —On Friday morning, shortly after dawn,Constable Whittaker and two keepers in the employ of the Duke of Devonshire met a gang of poachers coming from Chatsworth Park. A desperate encounter ensued, in which a policeman was knocked down and kicked; two poachers got away, and one was apprehended after a fierce resistance, in the course of which he was severely injured. MR, STEVENSON'S MOTION.—In the division on Mr. Francis Stevenson's motion on the Local Government Bill, the minority which supported the motion included seven Liberal Unionists, Mr. Chamberlain, Mr. Jesse Collins, Mr. Kenrick, Mr. Quilter, Mr. Gurdon, Mr. Archibald Corbett, and Mr. A. H. Brown • and two Con- servatives, Baron Dimsdale, and Mr. Stephens. The majority included 22,Liberal Upionists. THE SMALLPDX EPIDEMIC AT PRESTON. The fearful epidemic of smallpox which broke on Sun- day, at Preston, continues to spread with great rapidity. There were a number of new cases en Friday morning, bringing the total up to 161. On Friday a special meet- ing of the Board of Guardiads was held to confer with the representatives of the Corporation as to placing Jack- son Hospital. with its two hundred beds, in connection with the Fulwood Workhouse, at the disposal of the sani- tary authorities for the reception of cases. It is thought there are at least one hundred and eighty patients. The disease has spread since Sunday with appalling sudden- ness, and the three deaths recorded on Thursday were those of a middle-aged man, a girl of fourteen, and a baby. SEVEN LIVES LOST IN INDIA. Mail news from India on Friday states that at Simla it has been reported from Srinugger that an Englishman with six servants have been buried in an avalanche in Kaintal Nulla, in Kishtwar. YESTERDAY'S PARLIAMENT. ROUSE OF LORDS. The House met at 4 o'clock. SHIP CANAL, &c.—The Manchester Ship Canal Bill was read a third time, and passed. A bill to amend the Irish Pharmacy Act. 1875, was read a second time, and re- ferred to a Select Committee. CHINESE LABOUR.—The Earls Of CARNARVON and DUN- RAVEN drew attent!on to the action of the Australian colonies towards Chinese immigrants, and moved for returns ef correspondence and the Act passed by the colonial legislation.—Lord KNIITSFORD regretted the sud- den action of the New South Wales legislature in passing stringent regulations affecting Chinese immigrants. The question should be discussed at aConference tobe held on 12th inst. ; and he suggested that the motions for returns should stand over until the results of the Conferencewere known.—The Earl of DERBY said the real question was one of wages, and we should not interfere with the colonists. Thes motion were postponed, and the House shortly afterwards adjourned.' HOUSE OF COMMONS. The House met for a morning sitting, the fitst of a series to be held on Tuesdays and Fridays till the Local Government -tall is through Committee. The Speaker took the chair shortly after two o'clock. THE COMPENSATION CLAUSES.—Sir WILFRID LAWSON put a question to the Speaker from a point of order. (hp of the standing orders of the House provided that no member should be entitled to vote on any question in which he had a direct personal interest. He desired to know whether brewers would be entitled to vote upon the compensation clauses of the Local Government Bill. —The SPEAKER': That is a matter which is settled by the judgment of the House.—Mr. RITCHIE, replying to Mr, Summers, said a statement of the value of public-houses in this country had been prepared,' and would be issued in a few days. THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT BILL.—TOWN COUNTIES. At three o'clock the House went into committee on the Local Government Bill. On clause 1, which consti- tutes the county councils. Sir HENRY JAMES :brought for- ward an amendment to constitute every borough which contains 50,000 inhabitants, at the passing of the Act, a county by itself within the meaning of the bill—Mr. Marine upon this made animportant announcement. He said the Government would assent to the principle of the amendment, and constitute all towns ef 50,000 popu- lation and upwards separate comities. There were also a few boroughs of under 50,000 which they would admit to the priyilege of being counties by themselves if the boroughs themselves desired it. They were Exeter, Lincoln, Chester, Gloucester, Worcester, and Canter- bury. All towns that could prove they had 50,000 in- habitants at the time of the passing of the Act would be entitled to admission. In consequence of this change in the original form of the bill certain re-arrangements of the financial proposals would be necessary. He sugges- ted that Sir H. James should be satisfied with the assur- ance of the Government, and withdraw his amendment in the meantime. Sir W. FIAR- COURT expressed his satisfaction with , the con- cession which the Government had made. He wished .the amendment to be ma:de at once. Mr. RITCHIE urged the inconvenience of introducing the amendment in the first clause.—Mr. F. S. Powell. Sir U. Kay Shuttleworth, Sir S. Northcote, and Mr. H. Fowler in the discussion which followed, approved of the altera- tion made by the government. Sir H. James would withdraw the amenddment if it was clearly and expli- citly understood that the alteration would to Specifically carried out, and that the government would makeit a vital part of the Bill. Discussion then ensued as to the advisability of further reducing the limit below 50,000.— Mr. Marina said he could not hold out the slightest hope that the limit would be further reduced, and explained, lin answer to a question from Sir W. RARTTELOT, that it was proposed that the taxes to be given up to the counties in relief of Local Taxation should go into a common purse, and be distributed according to the rate- able value. The amendment was withdrawn and the clause was agreed to. OTHER AMENDMENTS. On clause 2, Mr. SCALE Hays, moved an amendment to the clause to provide that clergymen an ministers of religion should not be disqualified for being elected and acting as CountyCouncillors.—Mr. RITCHIE accepted the amendment, and it was agreed to. Mr. HOIIHOUSE moved an amendment to provide that a registered Parliamentary voter for county or division of county, in respect of the ownership of property, should be eligible for a councillor.—Mr.Fowrya and Mr. STANS- FELD raised objection tothe amendment, but Mr. RITCHIE assented to it. Several other proposals were discussed and objected to, after which the committee, divided on Mr. Hobhouse's original amendment, which was carried by 249 votes to 171.—The sitting was then suspended. The House res*ed at nine. Mr. KING called attention to the grievances of the un- covenanted European servants of the Government of India particularly, as regards leave, returning rules, and the payment of pensions. [LEFT SITTING.]
